title: Everything is ugly, so go build something that isn't — Raiza Martin, Huxe (ex NotebookLM)
talk_summary: A product-philosophy talk from the ex-NotebookLM PM about clarity, purpose, trust, and restraint when building AI products, illustrated with NotebookLM and Huxe anecdotes.

takeaways.what_they_do: Define the one outcome a product must deliver flawlessly every time, and use it to reject features that are novelty rather than core job.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what is the single outcome that your product has to deliver every time for every user flawlessly

takeaways.technique: Expose the edges / instrument worst case
takeaways.what_they_do: Design and instrument for failure paths, not just the happy path, and surface model limitations honestly rather than papering over them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: people are trying to instrument for like the best use case but not the worst case

takeaways.technique: Nail deterministic paths before probabilistic ones
takeaways.what_they_do: Ensure the boring deterministic parts of the app work reliably before adding model-driven delight.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have to nail the deterministic things before the delightful probabilistic bits

takeaways.technique: First-query / first-run success as the metric
takeaways.what_they_do: Track the most common first user action (90% of first queries were summarization) and treat failure there as fatal, since users don't return.
takeaways.evidence_quote: 90% of like users their first query was a summarization query

takeaways.what_they_do: Refuse to ship a pile of capabilities without a point of view; ask whether the product respects user time, data, and agency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the barrier to shipping, especially nowadays, it is not it's not about the capability, right? It's about judgment
